slot.brief: Elimination followed by HBr addition (Markovnikov/anti-Markovnikov with peroxide): trace the final product through a two-step sequence

stem: The major alkene formed by heating 2-bromo-2-methylbutane with alcoholic KOH is treated with HBr in the presence of peroxide. What is the final major product?

verdicts.working: Alcoholic KOH gives the more substituted alkene, 2-methylbut-2-ene. With HBr/peroxide, anti-Markovnikov addition places Br on the less substituted alkene carbon, giving 2-bromo-3-methylbutane.

working:
Elimination gives the major alkene, 2-methylbut-2-ene. With HBr/peroxide, Br adds to the less substituted alkene carbon: product = 2-bromo-3-methylbutane.

Independent check: Alcoholic KOH gives the more substituted alkene, 2-methylbut-2-ene. With HBr/peroxide, anti-Markovnikov addition places Br on the less substituted alkene carbon, giving 2-bromo-3-methylbutane.
solution:
Alcoholic KOH gives the more substituted alkene, 2-methylbut-2-ene. With HBr in the presence of peroxide, anti-Markovnikov addition places Br on the less substituted carbon:
$$\mathrm{CH_3C(CH_3)=CHCH_3 \xrightarrow{HBr,\,peroxide} CH_3CH(CH_3)CH(Br)CH_3}$$
The product is 2-bromo-3-methylbutane.
